title: Data-Driven Prediction of NaCl-Type Entropy-Stabilized Oxide Compositions from First-Principles and Supervised Learning
authors: Sebastien Junier, Celine Barreteau, David Berardan, Yann-Andrev Kerneur, Jean-Claude Crivello
abstract: Entropy-stabilized oxides (ESOs) open access to vast multicomponent compositional spaces, but identifying promising candidates remains challenging because of the large number of possible mixtures and the need to assess their stability against competing phases. In this work, we develop a high-throughput computational framework to screen equimolar quinary ESOs in the NaCl structure type by combining density functional theory (DFT), special quasirandom structures (SQS), convex-hull thermodynamics, and supervised machine learning. A consistent reference database of binary and ternary ordered oxides, including disordered phases such as all binary cation combinations in the NaCl-type oxide, is first constructed using GGA and meta-GGA calculations. Quinary disordered phases are then described by SQS supercells and used to train machine-learning models that predict the distance to the convex hull and the corresponding stabilization temperature over the full set of 4368 possible equimolar quinary compositions generated from 16 cation species. Among the tested models, an optimized multilayer perceptron provides the best predictive performance, with a test error of about 4 kJ/mol, while requiring explicit DFT calculations for only about 10% of the quinary systems. Comparison with experimental synthesis tests and computed decomposition paths further shows that the approach captures the main stability trends and the dominant competing phases, although absolute stabilization temperatures remain affected by systematic thermodynamic approximations. These results establish an efficient route for the data-driven exploration of multicomponent oxides and provide practical guidance for the experimental search for new ESOs.
summary: This work presents a computational framework that merges Density Functional Theory, Special Quasirandom Structures, and supervised Machine Learning to screen for stable Entropy-Stabilized Oxides. By training ML models on DFT data from thousands of potential compositions, the authors efficiently predict phase stability and guide experimentalists toward novel materials candidates.
main_problem: The primary challenge is identifying stable Entropy-Stabilized Oxide (ESO) compositions within vast, complex multicomponent spaces by accurately assessing their thermodynamic stability against competing phases.
main_result: The developed data-driven framework successfully screens thousands of potential quinary ESOs, providing a computationally efficient route to guide experimental synthesis efforts.
method: A high-throughput workflow combines first-principles DFT calculations (using SQS supercells) with supervised machine learning models (like MLP and Random Forest) trained to predict stability metrics.
model_or_system: The system under study is the $	ext{NaCl}$-type structure of quinary Entropy-Stabilized Oxides, $(\{M_i\})O$, involving up to 16 different cation species. Stability is assessed by calculating the formation enthalpy relative to the convex hull.
key_observables: Formation enthalpy deviation from the convex hull ($\Delta_{	ext{hull}}H$) and the stabilization temperature ($T_{	ext{stab}}$).
important_parameters: The test error for the optimized ML model was reported as $\approx 4 	ext{ kJ}\cdot	ext{mol}^{-1}$. The calculations cover up to quinary mixtures.
main_assumptions: Absolute stabilization temperatures are affected by systematic thermodynamic approximations, and magnetic ordering in the database was not fully optimized due to computational cost.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the performance of ML models (prediction vs. actual $\Delta_{	ext{hull}}H$) and show convergence tests for SQS supercell sizes and k-point meshes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem, details the combined DFT/SQS/ML methodology, presents results on screening thousands of compositions, and concludes by establishing an efficient data-driven search protocol for ESOs.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the core methodology—combining high-fidelity quantum simulations (DFT) with machine learning to predict complex many-body properties in disordered systems—is highly relevant to modeling strongly correlated or disordered quantum materials.
